# Tides at the north jetty

Spring tides at the north jetty run about two metres above the neap range,
and the sandbar off the eastern point uncovers roughly an hour either side of
low water. The published tide table is computed for the harbour mouth, not
for the jetty, and the jetty runs about eighteen minutes late on every
prediction.

The relieving boat cannot land at the jetty steps inside two hours of low
water on a spring tide, whatever the table says. Two crews learned that the
hard way in the same season before anyone wrote it down here.

Barometric pressure moves the actual height away from the prediction by a
useful rule of thumb: a centimetre of water for every hectopascal below the
seasonal mean. In a deep low the water arrives higher and earlier than the
table promises.
